title: Python SDK: attrs-first checkpointed streaming adapters and schema migration helpers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: The current Python SDK primarily documents dataclass/pydantic-first patterns for typed responses, which are heavy for minimal clients and create friction for generator-based streaming consumers. We need a lightweight, attrs-first adapter layer that: (1) supports generator/async-generator parsing of streaming LLM responses with checkpointed idempotent retry points, (2) provides migration helpers to handle schema evolution (add/remove fields, union flattening) with minimal runtime cost, and (3) exposes a thin Protocol-based API so downstream code can type against an interface rather than a concrete model implementation. This ticket implements the core adapters, tests, and a migration cookbook.
acceptance_criteria: Provide attrs-based model adapters that can be constructed from single-line JSON events emitted by the streaming endpoint
Implement a generator-friendly parse API: parse_stream(iterable[str]) -> Iterator[ModelProtocol] and an async variant
Checkpointing semantics: library emits stable checkpoint tokens at safe boundaries (after full model object assembly) and supports resume_from_checkpoint(token)
Migration helpers: a small utility that applies field rename maps and optional defaulting for removed fields when hydrating older responses
Comprehensive unit tests and golden snapshot tests for three schema evolution scenarios
Docs: short README + code examples and a demo notebook (link included)
implementation_notes: Design decision: use attrs for runtime-light, predictable init costs; provide optional pydantic bridge factory for teams that prefer validation-heavy models
Expose ModelProtocol (typing.Protocol) with minimal methods: .to_dict(), .checkpoint_boundary(), .from_event(event: dict) -> ModelProtocol
Checkpoint token format: base64 encoded JSON {v:1, seq: <event-seq>, model_sn: <sha1>} to remain compact and auditable
Parse algorithm: incremental event aggregator that yields on complete object boundary OR when explicit 'final_chunk' flag in event is true
Retry semantics: client retry should call resume_from_checkpoint and replay events since the checkpoint; SDK provides helper to compute minimal replay window based on token
Migration helper API: migrate_event(event: dict, mapping: dict[str,str], defaults: dict[str, Any]) -> dict
Performance: target <3% token-processing overhead vs raw json.loads on microbenchmarks for 8k tokens streams; bench harness recorded ~1.9% on 3090 baseline (see PR)

2026-03-11: Prototype committed: parse_stream generator and basic checkpoint token. Initial bench harness added (microbench/results/attrs-vs-json.md).
2026-03-12: Design review with PM (Ravi Patel) and DX lead (Marta Chen). Feedback: add pydantic bridge factory and explicit migration cookbook examples. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-13: Implemented migration helper and three migration scenarios (field rename, optional->required with default, union tag change). Added unit tests for each.
2026-03-14: Internal RFC posted and PR #8123 opened for initial review. Running CI and adding integration test against streaming simulator.
qa_plan: Unit tests cover parse behavior and migration helper cases. Add fuzz test that generates event permutations and validates idempotent resume behavior. Integration test will run a streaming simulator injecting network disconnect at random intervals and assert resume preserves semantics.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind sdk_preview flag. Roll out in two stages: (1) enable for internal Redwood services and run shadow traffic for 2 weeks, (2) opt-in beta customers. Monitor: dropped-events, successful-resumes, mean time to resume (MTTR).
